title: Little Hawley Rising Again
premise: Estate lawyer Juniper Eastwick is summoned to the decaying Hawley manor to read a will for a woman, Cordelia Hawley, who died eleven years ago—and whose death Juniper's own late mentor helped certify. Twin letters arrive: one confessing that Cordelia was murdered and that Juniper's mentor knew it, the other promising an inheritance to whoever uncovers the truth before the anniversary dinner. As Juniper navigates a household of resentful heirs, a groundskeeper who loved Cordelia, and her own growing bond with Cordelia's estranged daughter, she discovers her mentor falsified the death certificate to protect someone he loved. At the anniversary dinner, Juniper exposes the killer—Cordelia's husband, now frail and untouchable in his final months—who confesses quietly; the estate passes to the found family who tended its secrets, and Juniper chooses love over the invisible life she built.
about_author: S. M. Dravenmoor spent a decade as a probate clerk in coastal New England before turning to fiction, where the paperwork of the dead became the raw material of mystery. They write from a converted boathouse, accompanied by a one-eared cat named Probate.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Juniper Eastwick receives a certified letter requesting her presence at Hawley Manor to execute a will dated three days after Cordelia Hawley's death eleven years ago. Her POV establishes her careful, invisible life and her unease: the document is legally impossible. Emotional beat: dread dressed as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: At the manor, Juniper finds two sealed letters left with the housekeeper, both in Cordelia's hand—one confessing murder, one promising 'more than money' to whoever finishes what was started. POV alternates between Juniper and the housekeeper, Mrs. Vane. Emotional beat: the past reaching through paper to grab the present.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Juniper reviews the original probate file and discovers her mentor, Aldous Crane, signed the death certificate as attending witness—a role he had no legal right to play. His POV in flashback shows him burning a page of notes. Emotional beat: betrayal by the dead man who taught her everything.

chapters.title: The Heirs at the Gate
chapters.summary: The family gathers: Cordelia's brother-in-law Reginald, grasping and polished; her son Edmund, drinking; and her daughter Wren, returned after a decade abroad, sharp-tongued and grieving sideways. Juniper's POV as she interviews each heir. Emotional beat: a house full of people rehearsing innocence.

chapters.title: What the Groundskeeper Kept
chapters.summary: Juniper tracks down Tomas Reyes, the groundskeeper whose name appears in the second letter. He reveals he loved Cordelia and that she'd asked him to hide something in the greenhouse the week she died. His POV. Emotional beat: tenderness surviving under decades of fear.

chapters.title: The Greenhouse Ledger
chapters.summary: In the ruined greenhouse, Juniper and Wren find a hidden ledger recording payments from Cordelia to an unknown recipient—large sums, monthly, ending the week of her death. Shared POV chapter, first real alliance forming. Emotional beat: two lonely people discovering they trust each other more than their families.

chapters.title: Crane's Last Case
chapters.summary: Juniper searches her late mentor's office and finds a locked drawer keyed to Cordelia's birthday. Inside: the missing page of his notes and a photograph of Cordelia alive at a train station—dated four days after her official death. Juniper's POV. Emotional beat: vertigo; the case everyone closed was never closed.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: Reginald announces the family will hold the delayed eleventh-anniversary memorial dinner, pressuring Juniper to finalize the estate before then. Someone ransacks her guest room. Her POV, threaded with Mrs. Vane watching from the stairs. Emotional beat: the walls closing in, elegantly.

chapters.title: Wren's Version
chapters.summary: Wren tells Juniper about the night her mother died—the argument she overheard, the smell of burnt paper, her father's calm. She admits she fled England because no one would listen to a grieving child. Wren's POV. Emotional beat: grief finally given permission to speak.

chapters.title: The Confession Letter, Decoded
chapters.summary: Juniper realizes the confession letter is written in the shorthand code Cordelia used in her gardening journals. Decoded, it names no killer but says: 'He knows I know. If I drown, look to the pond.' Juniper's POV. Emotional beat: the dead woman finding her voice at last.

chapters.title: Dredging the Past
chapters.summary: Juniper and Tomas search the ornamental pond at night and recover a rusted strongbox containing Cordelia's real diary and a second, unsigned will leaving everything to Wren and Tomas. They are nearly caught by Edmund. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into danger.

chapters.title: Edmund's Debt
chapters.summary: Confronted, Edmund breaks down: his gambling debts were paid monthly by his mother—matching the ledger—but he swears he never touched her. He saw his father, Alistair, burning papers that night. Edmund's POV. Emotional beat: a weak man choosing, finally, to be honest.

chapters.title: Alistair Hawley, Dying
chapters.summary: Juniper visits Alistair, now terminally ill and lucid in a way he hasn't been in years. He neither confirms nor denies, but says: 'You'll want to ask Crane why he stayed silent.' His POV, cold and controlled. Emotional beat: the horror of a villain who has made peace with himself.

chapters.title: Why Crane Stayed Silent
chapters.summary: A final hidden letter from Crane, found in the firm's archive, explains: he discovered the truth years later but had already helped bury it, and exposing Alistair would have destroyed Wren's inheritance and his own reputation. He chose duty to the living over justice for the dead—and hated himself for it. Crane's POV. Emotional beat: tragic complicity, mirrored in Juniper's own choices.

chapters.title: Someone Burns the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: The greenhouse burns overnight, destroying remaining evidence. Mrs. Vane is found unconscious nearby—silenced or framed? Juniper suspects Reginald, who has been oddly knowledgeable about her movements. Juniper's POV. Emotional beat: escalation; the killer is done being subtle.

chapters.title: Mrs. Vane Wakes
chapters.summary: Mrs. Vane recovers enough to reveal she saw Alistair at the pond the night Cordelia died, and that Reginald paid her for years to keep quiet about small oddities—Cordelia's 'travels,' the locked study. Her POV. Emotional beat: the servants' loyalty to Cordelia outweighing fear at last.

chapters.title: Reginald's Gambit
chapters.summary: Reginald threatens Juniper professionally—her license, her firm, her mentor's posthumous reputation—if she pursues the matter before the dinner. He offers her a partnership. Juniper's POV as she weighs invisibility against truth. Emotional beat: temptation offered in a velvet glove.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Juniper and Wren, up all night assembling evidence, admit what's growing between them. Wren asks her not to come to the dinner if it costs her everything; Juniper refuses to hide again. Shared intimate POV. Emotional beat: love declared on the eve of ruin.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: At the memorial dinner, Juniper rises during the toast and presents the diary, ledger, and testimony. Alistair, wheeled in against medical advice, listens without expression. The room fractures—Reginald denies, Edmund confirms, Wren stands with her. Juniper's POV. Emotional beat: the climax; a glass raised to a lie, shattered.

chapters.title: A Quiet Confession
chapters.summary: Privately, Alistair confesses to Juniper alone: Cordelia discovered he'd been embezzling the estate and planned to expose him; they argued at the pond and she fell; he let the water do the rest, and bought Crane's silence out of desperation, not malice. He will die within months, beyond any court. His POV. Emotional beat: justice arriving too late to satisfy, but not too late to matter.

chapters.title: The Second Will Stands
chapters.summary: Juniper executes the true will: the manor goes to Wren and Tomas jointly, with provision for Mrs. Vane. Reginald retreats, discredited; Edmund enters recovery. Juniper faces a disciplinary inquiry over her methods but keeps her license—and her integrity. Her POV. Emotional beat: the cost paid, the case truly closed.

chapters.title: Little Hawley Rising Again
chapters.summary: One year later, the manor is restored, its gardens replanted under Tomas's hands. Wren and Juniper host a spring dinner—not an anniversary of death but of beginning. On the table sit Cordelia's twin letters, framed: confession and promise, both kept. Shared closing POV. Emotional beat: found family, love chosen over duty, and a house that breathes again.
